quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Watch your lips in a mirror at the start. Do they close, or stay open while the tongue moves?
quests.explanation: 'Bell' starts with /b/, a lip sound: both lips seal and release with the voice on. The tongue-tip alternative, /d/, involves no lip movement at all, since the tongue taps the ridge while the lips stay open, and you'd get 'dell'. Checking the lips separates the two places instantly.
quests.mouthPosition: Close both lips with your voice on and release softly. The tongue stays low until the vowel needs it, and only lifts later for the 'l'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Both hums travel through your nose. To decide, notice the end of the word: do your lips close, or do they stay slightly open?
quests.explanation: 'Moon' begins with /m/ and ends with /n/. The start closes the lips; the ending doesn't, because the tongue tip rises to the ridge while the lips relax open. If your lips close again at the end you've said 'moom'. It's a handy word for feeling the two places back to back.
quests.mouthPosition: At the end, lift your tongue tip to the ridge behind your top teeth, hum through your nose, and leave your lips relaxed and slightly apart.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Freeze right at the end of the word. Are your lips sealed, or is the tip of your tongue touching behind your top teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Soup' ends in /p/: the lips shut and stop the air with no voice. A tongue-tip ending, /t/, would make the word 'suit'. The vowel is identical in both, so only the place of the final closure separates them, and the lips are the visible one.
quests.mouthPosition: Close on a firm lip seal at the last sound with your voice off, then either release a tiny puff or hold the closure.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Check what your bottom lip does at the start. Does it press against the top lip, or slide back to touch your upper teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Food' begins with /f/, a lip-and-teeth sound: the lower lip touches the upper teeth and air hisses out. /p/ uses both lips and pops. A simple check: if your top teeth are resting on your lower lip, it's /f/; if they're clear of it, it's a two-lip sound.
quests.mouthPosition: Rest your upper teeth on your lower lip and push a smooth stream of air across it with your voice off.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The last sound is made at the lips. Do your two lips meet each other, or does your bottom lip touch your upper teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Wave' ends in /v/: the lip touches the upper teeth and air buzzes through. The lip-to-lip alternative is /b/, which would give 'wabe'. The final E is silent, so the mouth movement at the end is your only clue.
quests.mouthPosition: Glide out of the 'ay' vowel and rest your top teeth on your bottom lip at the end with your voice on and air buzzing through.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: In the middle of the word, do the two lips press together, or does the lower lip lift toward the teeth? Feel the moment between the syllables.
quests.explanation: 'Happy' has /p/ in the middle: both lips seal and release with a tiny puff. If your lower lip slides up to your teeth you'll say 'haffy'. The double P in the spelling is still just one sound.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'ha-', press both lips together firmly with your voice off and release into the final 'ee' vowel.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Notice how far your tongue travels between the start and the end of this word. Where does it finish?
quests.explanation: 'Coat' begins with /k/, made with the back of the tongue, and ends with /t/, made with the tip. The tongue has to travel forward, which is the step many learners skip. Finish at the back and you'll say 'coak'. Feel the tip land behind your top teeth.
quests.mouthPosition: Straight after the 'oh', lift your tongue tip to the ridge behind your upper teeth and stop the air, with your voice off.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say only the first sound and feel where the tongue touches. Is it against the ridge behind your teeth, or far back near your throat?
quests.explanation: 'Gate' starts with /g/, made at the back of the mouth: the back of the tongue lifts to the soft palate while the voice runs. The front sound /d/ would give 'date'. Both are voiced, so buzzing can't help you here; only the tongue's location can.
quests.mouthPosition: Lift the back of your tongue to the soft palate with your voice on, then release smoothly into 'ate' while the tongue tip stays low.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Between the two syllables, which part of your tongue lifts? Feel for it: front or back?
quests.explanation: 'Bacon' has /k/ in the middle, made with the back of the tongue against the soft palate. A tongue-tip version would drift toward 'bayton'. The sound sits in the middle of the word, so keep it firm rather than swallowing it.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'bay-', lift the back of your tongue against the soft palate with your voice off, then release into the short 'en'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Look at your lips in a mirror on the first sound. Are they rounded and pushed slightly forward, or spread as in a smile?
quests.explanation: 'Shop' begins with /ʃ/. The tongue pulls back a little from the ridge and the lips round, giving a broader, softer hiss than /s/. If you hear a thin, high hiss, you've slid into /s/ and the word becomes 'sop'.
quests.mouthPosition: Pull your tongue slightly back from the ridge, round and push your lips forward a little, and blow a broad stream of air with your voice off.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Smile slightly and stretch the first sound. Is the hiss thin and high, or broad and soft?
quests.explanation: 'Sock' begins with /s/: tongue tip forward near the ridge, teeth close together, lips spread, and a thin, high hiss. /ʃ/ pulls the tongue back and rounds the lips for a duller sound, which would turn the word into 'shock', a big change in meaning.
quests.mouthPosition: Bring your tongue tip close behind your upper teeth, spread your lips, and push a narrow channel of air through. Keep it tight and bright.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word begins with the letter S, but say it aloud and check where your tongue and lips are. Thin hiss or broad hush?
quests.explanation: 'Sugar' starts with /ʃ/ despite the S in the spelling. Only a few everyday words do this, and 'sugar' is the one you'll use most. Start it with /s/ and listeners hear something slightly off, even if they understand you.
quests.mouthPosition: Pull your tongue slightly back, round your lips, and blow a broad hush before the short vowel. Save the /g/ for the middle.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word ends with a hiss. Stretch it: does your tongue sit forward, or draw back with your lips rounding?
quests.explanation: 'Wash' ends in /ʃ/, the broad hush. A common slip is finishing with a thin /s/ and saying 'wass', especially in fast speech. Hold the ending a moment longer with rounded lips and the word sounds complete.
quests.mouthPosition: End with your tongue pulled slightly back, lips rounded a little, and a broad voiceless stream of air.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Don't trust the CH in the spelling. Say the middle sound slowly: is it thin and high, or broad and soft?
quests.explanation: 'Machine' has /ʃ/ in the middle. That CH spelling shows up in words borrowed from French, such as 'chef'. The tongue pulls back and the lips round for a broad hush. A thin /s/ would turn it into 'massine' and lose the stress pattern.
quests.mouthPosition: After the short 'muh', pull your tongue slightly back, round your lips, and hush air through before the stressed 'een'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: The word ends with the letters CE. Stretch the last sound: is it thin and bright, or broad and soft?
quests.explanation: 'Notice' ends in /s/; the letters CE stand for a plain /s/ here. The tongue tip stays forward with the lips spread. Pulling the tongue back gives /ʃ/, which sounds like 'notish' and is much less clear.
quests.mouthPosition: In the last syllable, keep your tongue tip near the ridge behind your top teeth, lips spread, and blow a thin voiceless hiss.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Don't listen for a 'g' at the end. Say the word slowly and feel the back of your tongue. Does it press up while the sound hums through your nose?
quests.explanation: 'King' ends in /ŋ/, a single nasal made at the back of the tongue, with no separate /g/ afterwards. The back of the tongue stays against the soft palate and the sound hums through the nose. If the tip goes up instead you get 'kin', a different word.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate, keep the tongue tip low, and hum through your nose without releasing into a 'g'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: At the end of the word, where is the tip of your tongue: down behind your bottom teeth, or lifted to the ridge?
quests.explanation: 'Run' ends in /n/: tongue tip up on the ridge and voiced air through the nose. /ŋ/ would send the back of the tongue up and sound like 'rung'. It's a tip-versus-back contrast, so feel where the tongue lands.
quests.mouthPosition: Finish with your tongue tip resting on the ridge behind your upper teeth and hum through your nose.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: This word has a nasal in the middle and another at the end. Focus on the final one: is it made with the tongue tip or the back?
quests.explanation: 'Morning' has /n/ in the middle and /ŋ/ at the end. The -ING ending is one sound. Casual speech often uses the tongue tip there, but in clear, careful speech the back of the tongue should rise to the soft palate.
quests.mouthPosition: In the last syllable, raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate and hum through your nose, without adding a 'g'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Check whether your top teeth touch your bottom lip when the word begins. Is there any contact?
quests.explanation: 'West' starts with /w/: lips rounded and pushed forward, then opening quickly into the vowel, with no contact between teeth and lip. /v/ would touch the lip to the teeth and give 'vest'. If your teeth touch your lip on the first sound, it isn't /w/.
quests.mouthPosition: Round your lips as if to whistle, then open quickly into 'est'. Keep your teeth clear of your lower lip.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Look in a mirror: at the start, does the lower lip touch the upper teeth, or do the lips round forward?
quests.explanation: 'Very' starts with /v/: upper teeth on the lower lip with a buzz. Rounding the lips instead gives /w/ and 'werry', a classic swap. Teeth on lip is the clear check.
quests.mouthPosition: Set your top teeth on your bottom lip, voice on, and hold a short buzz before the 'e'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Which start has your two lips firmly meeting, and which only rounds them? Check the very first movement.
quests.explanation: 'Book' begins with /b/, where both lips seal completely and then release. The /w/ alternative only rounds the lips without closing them, so it flows straight into the vowel: 'wook'. A full seal followed by a release is your clue.
quests.mouthPosition: Press your lips together to seal them completely with your voice on, then open softly into the short 'oo' vowel.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Hold the hum at the end of the word. Can you open your lips while it continues?
quests.explanation: 'Room' ends in /m/: the lips seal and voiced air exits through the nose. Lifting the tongue tip instead gives /n/ and 'roon'. Keeping the lips closed for a beat at the end is what sells the /m/.
quests.mouthPosition: Finish by closing both lips and humming through your nose. Let the sound fade.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Freeze at the end of the word. Are your lips touching, or is the back of your tongue lifted?
quests.explanation: 'Bike' ends in /k/, made at the back of the tongue: it lifts to the soft palate and stops the air with no voice. Ending on the lips instead gives /p/, a word English doesn't have, so listeners struggle to place it.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of your tongue against the soft palate at the end, with your voice off. A small puff is optional.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: At the very end, is the closure made with your lips or with the tip of your tongue?
quests.explanation: 'Hot' ends in /t/: the tongue tip stops the air against the ridge with no voice. Closing the lips would give 'hop', a different word. The tongue tip's landing spot, just behind the top teeth, is the marker.
quests.mouthPosition: Tap the tongue tip up behind the upper teeth to cut off the air, voice off.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Say the first sound with your lips slightly apart. Can you still make it, or do the lips have to meet?
quests.explanation: 'Key' starts with /k/, made at the back of the tongue with the lips free, so you can produce it with your lips open the whole time. The /p/ option needs the lips shut and would give 'pea'. Lips open versus lips shut separates them.
quests.mouthPosition: Lift the back of your tongue to the soft palate and release with a puff, keeping your lips slightly spread for the 'ee'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: At the end of the word, feel where the tongue is when the sound stops. Tip up at the front, or back lifted?
quests.explanation: 'Road' ends in /d/: the tongue tip presses the ridge with the voice on. A back-of-tongue ending would be /g/, which is also voiced, so the buzz can't help. Only the location of the tongue tells them apart.
quests.mouthPosition: Finish by touching your tongue tip to the ridge behind your upper teeth with your voice running, then let it fade.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: In the middle of the word, do your lips come together, or does your tongue tip lift?
quests.explanation: 'Summer' has /m/ in the middle: the lips seal and voiced air flows through the nose, then the lips open for the final vowel. Using the tongue tip instead would give 'sunner'. Keep the lip closure for the hum.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'su-', close both lips and hum through your nose, then open into the weak final syllable.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE END OF THE WORD
quests.hint: Ignore the final G in the spelling. Where does your tongue end up: tip forward, or back raised?
quests.explanation: 'Long' ends with /ŋ/, a back-of-tongue nasal with no /g/ release. If the tongue tip rises instead you get 'lawn'. Two different words, separated only by where the tongue lands.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of your tongue to the soft palate and let the hum go through your nose, with no release.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND AT THE START OF THE WORD
quests.hint: At the start, look for contact: lip to lip, or lip to teeth?
quests.explanation: 'Vest' starts with /v/: lip on teeth with a buzz. /b/ would seal both lips and make it 'best', a meaningful pair when you're talking about clothes. The lip-teeth contact is the check.
quests.mouthPosition: Set your top teeth on your bottom lip, switch your voice on, and let the air buzz before moving to 'est'.

quests.instruction: IDENTIFY THE CONSONANT SOUND IN THE MIDDLE OF THE WORD
quests.hint: In the middle of the word, notice which part of the tongue is lifted: the tip forward, or the back?
quests.explanation: 'Pocket' has /k/ in the middle, formed at the back of the tongue, followed by a light /t/ at the end. The middle stop isn't made with the tip; a tongue-tip version gives something like 'potted'. The two stops sit in different places: back, then tip.
quests.mouthPosition: After 'pock-', lift the back of your tongue against the soft palate with your voice off, then bring the tip up for the final 't'.
